{{Short description|Theoretical physicist}}

'''Galileo Violini''' is a theoretical physicist and the director emeritus of the {{ill|Centro Internacional de Física|es}} in [[Bogotá]], Colombia. He is the recipient of the 2024 Joseph A. Burton Forum Award "for establishing programs in physics education and research in Latin America and the Caribbean that increased regional scientific capacity, for promoting international scientific cooperation across continents and regions of the world, and for creating the Centro Internacional de Física in Colombia."<ref name=aps>{{citation|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/award/burton-forum-award|title=Joseph A. Burton Forum Award|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|website=aps.org|access-date=2024-06-12|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612105241/https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/award/burton-forum-award|archive-date=2024-06-12}}</ref>

His main area of interests are [[science education]], [[science diplomacy]], and [[synchrotron|synchrotron science]]. He is participating in the project to bring a synchrotron light source to the [[Caribbean|Greater Caribbean]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1038/d41586-024-00598-4 |title=Big science in Latin America: Accelerate particles and progress |year=2024 |last1=Castaño |first1=Victor M. |last2=De Córdoba |first2=Pedro Fernández |last3=Sans |first3=Juan A. |last4=Violini |first4=Galileo |journal=Nature |volume=627 |issue=8002 |pages=32–34 |pmid=38438544 |bibcode=2024Natur.627...32C |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Violini graduated from [[La Sapienza University]] in [[Rome]], [[Italy]], in 1965, and obtained the Italian [[Libera docenza]] in theoretical physics from Sapienza in 1971, where he later became a professor of algebra and mathematical methods of physics. He then became a professor of [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Calabria]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twas.org/sites/default/files/twas_comsats_cif.pdf |title=Centro Internacional de Fisica – The World Academy of Science (UNESCO)}}</ref>

In 1985 he founded the International Center for Physics of Bogotá ({{lang|es|Centro Internacional de Física}}, CIF), in [[Colombia]], modeled on the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]],<ref name=ictp>{{cite web|url=https://www.ictp.it/home/spirit-abdus-salam-award-winners-2016 |title=Spirit of Abdus Salam Award Winners 2016 – International Center for Theoretical Physics|publisher=[[ICTP]]|website=ictp.it|access-date=2024-06-12}}</ref> where he is a director emeritus.{{r|aps}}

== Awards and honors ==
* 2023 John Wheatley Award of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/award/john-wheatley-award|title=John Wheatley Award|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|website=aps.org|access-date=2024-06-12|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612110021/https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/award/john-wheatley-award|archive-date=2024-06-12}}</ref>
* 2023 [[World Academy of Art and Science]] Fellow{{r|aps}}
* Honorary member of the [[Colombian Academy of Exact, Physical and Natural Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://worldscienceforum.org/speakers/violini-galileo-52569 |title=Galileo Violini biography – World Science Forum}}</ref>
* Outstanding Salvadorean Recognition from the Government of El Salvador<ref name=aps2>{{citation|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Violini&first_nm=Galileo&year=2024|title=2024 Joseph A. Burton Forum Award Recipient|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|website=aps.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221020006/https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Violini&first_nm=Galileo&year=2024|archive-date=2024-02-21}}</ref>
* 2016 Abdus Salam Spirit Award of the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]]{{r|ictp}}
* [[UNESCO]] Representative to Islamic Republic of Iran{{r|aps2}}
